scope: Shared persistent native edge and face input highlights in feature previews, independent of hover and result geometry
Failed input sets retain red boundary outlines and face tint, populated selection fields receive aria-invalid, and the feature tree receives a temporary error indication
Correction restores the configured selection color; cancel clears temporary feedback; missing or ambiguous face references never highlight a nearby unrelated face
Whole-face constant-radius Fillet and equal-distance Chamfer retry native contour order and two-pass corners, preserving every selected boundary and the exact requested size
Every finishing result must pass native BRep validity checking
Native topology cache identity, candidate face IDs, exact torus center and signed-zero snapshot equivalence

topology.result: 11 passed: equal-centroid/equal-area distinct faces, submicron placement, cache ID remapping, plane/cylinder/sphere/ellipse/torus/BSpline/Bezier boundaries and exact transformed torus frames

checks: Select either conical face through a real pointer click for Fillet and Chamfer

qualification.modeling_fixture_repair: Return to isometric view before locating Hole points; drag an overlapping feature window by its actual header instead of disabling pointer events. Original strict modeling assertions remain enabled.

limits: Kernel failures identify the failed input set, not necessarily one proven bad edge within that set; the UI does not claim otherwise
This shared native edge/face feedback does not establish complete Onshape parity or universal sketch/body-reference visualization
Variable-radius, width-based, unequal-distance and angle-based finishing never silently fall back to constant-size intent
Missing and ambiguous references still require correction rather than proximity-based reassignment
The earlier intermittent broad-modeling failure is not proven explained by the current passing gate
